headline: Himlung avalanche toll rises to seven dead, nine Nepali workers still missing
dek: Three bodies were recovered Wednesday, and outlets credited three different people with the update, leaving unclear who owns the official count.
body_markdown:
Three more bodies came off Himlung Himal on Wednesday, September 30. That brought the confirmed death toll from Sunday's avalanche to seven, with nine people still missing, Manang Chief District Officer Mukti Prasad Khanal said, according to The Rising Nepal and OnlineKhabar English News.

All nine still missing are Nepali nationals, PTI, the Indian news agency, reported, citing officials. They are mountain guides and kitchen staff, part of a group of 22 workers who travelled from Kathmandu to the 7,126 metre peak in Manang's Nar Phu area about two weeks earlier to fix ropes and prepare the base camp for the autumn climbing season, ETV Bharat reported. Separate ETV Bharat coverage used 22 as an early missing count, which authorities corrected on Tuesday, September 29.

For nine Nepali families, Thursday, October 1, brings no answers yet. The three bodies recovered on Wednesday, September 30, those of Aash Gurung, 58, of Gorkha, Suraj Rai, 21, of Khotang, and Kalam Budha, 57, of Rukum, are scheduled to be flown from Chame to Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu on Thursday morning, Nepalnews reported, citing Assistant Chief District Officer Krishna Prasad Paudel. Four other workers died earlier in the week. Chhebi Bhote and Pasang Bhote were recovered on Sunday, September 27, the day of the avalanche. Birendra Gurung and Ghanshyam Rai were recovered the next day, Monday, September 28, HimalPress reported.

The avalanche struck on Sunday morning amid heavy rain and snow that also set off landslides and floods elsewhere in Nepal, PTI reported. A weather warning had gone out the week before, and rope-fixing teams had begun pulling off the mountain, expedition organiser Mingma Gyalje Sherpa said, as reported by Daily Pioneer. Some people stayed behind despite the worsening conditions, he said.

At least two companies employed the workers. Himalayan Holidays Nepal and Imagine Nepal Pvt Ltd, which Nepalnews calls Expedition Imagine Company, confirmed on the day of the avalanche that eight and two of their staff respectively were unaccounted for, Expedition Operators Association general secretary Rishi Bhandari told the Kathmandu Post, as reported by Daily Pioneer. By Monday, September 28, the combined toll stood at four dead and 12 missing, sixteen in all, a total that has held since. Wednesday's count of seven dead and nine missing still adds to sixteen.

A 14-member rescue team remains on the mountain, PTI reported. The Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, NNMGA, says its search is being led by IFMGA-certified guides Pasang Kaji Sherpa and Bikram Karki, supported by five more guides, HimalPress reported. It is not clear from the reports reviewed whether the seven NNMGA guides are part of the 14 member team PTI described or a separate group.

## What the coverage missed

Three different voices have announced Wednesday's update, and it is not clear which one owns the official count. The Rising Nepal and OnlineKhabar name Manang CDO Mukti Prasad Khanal as the source of the toll. Nepalnews instead quotes Assistant CDO Krishna Prasad Paudel on the body transfers, and separately quotes NNMGA president Tul Singh Gurung saying "We have recovered three bodies from the avalanche today." HimalPress credits the NNMGA, not the district office, with coordinating the search itself.

## What we still do not know

The nine still missing have not been named individually in any report reviewed for this story. The Manang District Administration Office could release a full list.

Whether the weather warning issued before September 27 changed how many workers stayed on the mountain is unaddressed in the reports reviewed. The Department of Tourism could answer that.

No report reviewed says whether the dead or missing carried high-altitude worker insurance, or whether Himalayan Holidays Nepal and Imagine Nepal Pvt Ltd have paid the nine families anything while they wait. The Department of Tourism and the two companies could answer that.

social_hook: Seven Nepali guides and cooks are confirmed dead and nine more are missing after an avalanche buried their Himlung Himal camp, officials say.
take: Seven Nepali mountain workers are dead and nine more are missing on Himlung Himal, four days after an avalanche buried their camp. They were fixing ropes and cooking for climbers, not climbing for themselves. A weather warning went out before the slide hit, and some crews stayed anyway, expedition organiser Mingma Gyalje Sherpa said. Outlets have credited Manang's chief district officer, his assistant and the mountain guides' association with Wednesday's update, and it is unclear who owns the official count. Nine families now wait for a name.

The dead and missing were guides and kitchen staff, preparing the base camp for the autumn season. A weather warning went out before the avalanche struck on September 27. Some crews stayed behind anyway, expedition organiser Mingma Gyalje Sherpa said. Outlets credit three different people with the update. It is unclear who owns the official count. No report says whether the workers carried insurance. The three bodies found Wednesday are due at Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu on Thursday, Nepalnews reported.

nepali.headline: हिमलुङ हिमालमा मृत्यु ७ पुग्यो, ९ कामदार अझै बेपत्ता
nepali.dek: बुधबार थप तीन शव भेटिए, तर सञ्चारमाध्यमले अपडेटको श्रेय तीन फरक व्यक्तिलाई दिँदा आधिकारिक संख्या कसको हो भन्ने अस्पष्ट छ।
nepali.take: हिमलुङ हिमालमा हिमपहिरोले शिविर पुरेको चार दिनपछि सात नेपाली कामदारको मृत्यु पुष्टि भएको छ। नौ जना अझै बेपत्ता छन्। उनीहरू आफैं चढ्न होइन, अरूको आरोहणका लागि डोरी बाँध्न र खाना पकाउन हिमालमा गएका थिए। हिमपहिरो आउनुअघि नै मौसम चेतावनी जारी भइसकेको थियो, तैपनि केही टोली हिमालमै बसे, अभियान सञ्चालक मिङमा ग्याल्जे शेर्पाले भने। सञ्चारमाध्यमले बुधबारको अपडेटको श्रेय मनाङका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी, सहायक प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी र पर्वतीय गाइड संघलाई दिएका छन्। आधिकारिक तथ्यांक कसको हो भन्ने अझै स्पष्ट छैन। नौ परिवार अहिले आफन्तको नाम सुन्न कुरेर बसेका छन्।
nepali.body_markdown:
काठमाडौं । हिमलुङ हिमालमा आइतबार (२७ सेप्टेम्बर) गएको हिमपहिरोपछि बुधबार (३० सेप्टेम्बर) थप तीन शव फेला परेका छन्। द राइजिङ नेपाल र अनलाइनखबर इङ्लिस न्युजका अनुसार मनाङका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी मुक्तिप्रसाद खनालले मृतकको संख्या सात पुगेको र नौ जना अझै बेपत्ता रहेको बताएका छन्।

बेपत्ता सबै नौ जना नेपाली नागरिक रहेको अधिकारीहरूलाई उद्धृत गर्दै भारतीय समाचार संस्था पीटीआईले जनाएको छ। ईटीभी भारतका अनुसार उनीहरू पर्वतीय गाइड र भान्साका कर्मचारी हुन्। उनीहरू २२ जना कामदारको समूहमा थिए भनी ईटीभी भारतले लेखेको छ। यो समूह करिब दुई साता अगाडि काठमाडौंबाट मनाङको नार फू क्षेत्रमा रहेको ७,१२६ मिटर अग्लो हिमलुङ हिमालमा डोरी बाँध्न र शरद यामको आरोहणका निम्ति आधार शिविर तयार पार्न पुगेको थियो, ईटीभी भारतले नै जनाएको छ। ईटीभी भारतकै अर्को समाचारले सुरुमा बेपत्ताको संख्या २२ लेखेको थियो। ईटीभी भारतका अनुसार अधिकारीहरूले मंगलबार (२९ सेप्टेम्बर) त्यो संख्या सच्याए।

बिहीबार (१ अक्टोबर) सम्म पनि नौ नेपाली परिवारले आफन्तको कुनै खबर पाएका छैनन्। नेपालन्युजका अनुसार बुधबार फेला परेका तीन शव गोरखाका ५८ वर्षीय आश गुरुङ, खोटाङका २१ वर्षीय सूरज राई र रुकुमका ५७ वर्षीय कलम बुढाका हुन्। सहायक प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी कृष्णप्रसाद पौडेलले यी शव बिहीबार बिहान चामेदेखि काठमाडौंको त्रिभुवन विश्वविद्यालय शिक्षण अस्पतालसम्म हवाई मार्गबाट पुर्‍याइने बताएको नेपालन्युजले लेखेको छ। बाँकी चार जनाको मृत्यु हप्ताको सुरुतिरै भइसकेको थियो। हिमालप्रेसका अनुसार छेबी भोटे र पासाङ भोटेको शव हिमपहिरो परेकै दिन आइतबार फेला परेको थियो। वीरेन्द्र गुरुङ र घनश्याम राईको शव भोलिपल्ट सोमबार (२८ सेप्टेम्बर) भेटिएको थियो, हिमालप्रेसले जनाएको छ।

पीटीआईका अनुसार आइतबार बिहान भारी वर्षा र हिमपातकै बेला हिमपहिरो गएको थियो। त्यही वर्षा र हिमपातले देशका अन्य भागमा पहिरो र बाढी ल्याएको पीटीआईले उल्लेख गरेको छ। डेली पायोनियरका अनुसार अभियान सञ्चालक मिङमा ग्याल्जे शेर्पाले हिमपहिरोभन्दा अघिल्लो साता मौसम चेतावनी जारी भएको र डोरी बाँध्ने टोलीहरू हिमाल छाड्न थालिसकेको बताएका छन्। अवस्था बिग्रँदै गए पनि केही कामदार हिमालमै बसे, उनले भने।

हिमालयन होलिडेज नेपाल र इमेजिन नेपाल प्रालिसहित कम्तीमा २ कम्पनीले यी कामदारलाई काममा लगाएका थिए। नेपालन्युजले इमेजिन नेपाललाई एक्स्पिडिसन इमेजिन कम्पनी भनेको छ। डेली पायोनियरका अनुसार एक्स्पिडिसन अपरेटर्स एसोसिएसनका महासचिव ऋषि भण्डारीले हिमपहिरो परेकै दिन हिमालयन होलिडेज नेपालले आफ्ना ८ र इमेजिन नेपालले २ कर्मचारी बेपत्ता भएको पुष्टि गरेको द काठमाडौं पोस्टलाई बताएका थिए। सोमबार (२८ सेप्टेम्बर) सम्म ४ जनाको मृत्यु भएको र १२ जना बेपत्ता रहेको थियो। यो कुल १६ जनाको संख्या अहिलेसम्म उस्तै छ। बुधबारको ७ मृत्यु र ९ बेपत्ताको जोड पनि १६ नै हुन्छ।

हिमालमा अहिले पनि १४ सदस्यीय उद्धार टोली खटिएको छ, पीटीआईले जनाएको छ। हिमालप्रेसका अनुसार नेपाल राष्ट्रिय पर्वतीय गाइड संघ एनएनएमजिएले खोजीको नेतृत्व अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय प्रमाणपत्र पाएका आईएफएमजिए गाइड पासाङ काजी शेर्पा र विक्रम कार्कीले गरिरहेको जनाएको छ। थप ५ गाइडले उनीहरूलाई सघाइरहेको संघले जनाएको हिमालप्रेसले लेखेको छ। पीटीआईले उल्लेख गरेको १४ सदस्यीय टोलीमा यी ७ एनएनएमजिए गाइड पर्छन् कि पर्दैनन् भन्ने हामीले हेरेका कुनै समाचारमा खुलेको छैन।

## समाचारले छुटाएको कुरा

बुधबारको अपडेट तीन फरक स्रोतले सार्वजनिक गरेका छन्, र आधिकारिक संख्या कसको हो भन्ने स्पष्ट छैन। द राइजिङ नेपाल र अनलाइनखबरले मनाङका प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी मुक्तिप्रसाद खनाललाई यो संख्याको स्रोत भनेका छन्। नेपालन्युजले भने शव ढुवानीबारे सहायक प्रमुख जिल्ला अधिकारी कृष्णप्रसाद पौडेललाई उद्धृत गरेको छ। सोही सञ्चारमाध्यमले एनएनएमजिएका अध्यक्ष तुलसिंह गुरुङको भनाइ छुट्टै राखेको छ, "हामीले आज हिमपहिरोबाट तीनवटा शव निकालेका छौं।" हिमालप्रेसले भने खोजी अभियानको समन्वय जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयले होइन, एनएनएमजिएले गरिरहेको जनाएको छ।

## अझै थाहा नभएका कुरा

बेपत्ता नौ जनाको नाम यस प्रतिवेदनका लागि हेरिएका कुनै पनि रिपोर्टमा अलग अलग उल्लेख भएको छैन। मनाङ जिल्ला प्रशासन कार्यालयले पूरा सूची सार्वजनिक गर्न सक्छ।

२७ सेप्टेम्बर अघि जारी मौसम चेतावनीले कति कामदार हिमालमै बसे भन्नेमा कुनै असर पार्‍यो कि पारेन भन्ने कुरा यस प्रतिवेदनका लागि हेरिएका रिपोर्टमा उल्लेख छैन। पर्यटन विभागले यसको जवाफ दिन सक्छ।

मृतक वा बेपत्ताले उच्च हिमाली क्षेत्र कामदार बिमा गरेका थिए कि थिएनन्, वा हिमालयन होलिडेज नेपाल र इमेजिन नेपाल प्रालिले पर्खिरहेका नौ परिवारलाई अहिलेसम्म केही रकम बुझाएका छन् कि छैनन् भन्ने कुरा यस प्रतिवेदनका लागि हेरिएको कुनै रिपोर्टमा छैन। पर्यटन विभाग र उक्त दुई कम्पनीले यसको जवाफ दिन सक्छन्।

angles.claim: Coverage anchored on Rising Nepal/Nepalnews quotes Manang CDO Mukti Prasad Khanal as the sole voice announcing the toll, but Nepalnews's own detailed dispatch on the same update credits Assistant CDO Krishna Prasad Paudel, and HimalPress credits the Nepal National Mountain Guides Association (NNMGA) with coordinating the rescue rather than the district office — three different authorities for one official count.
angles.why_it_matters: If it is unclear which office actually owns the casualty count, it is unclear who is accountable for getting it right, for notifying the nine missing families, and for any eventual compensation decision.

evidence.fact: Credits Manang CDO Mukti Prasad Khanal with announcing that three more bodies were recovered on September 30, putting the toll at seven dead and nine missing.
Attributes the September 30 update to Assistant CDO Krishna Prasad Paudel rather than CDO Khanal.
Attributes rescue coordination to the Nepal National Mountain Guides Association (NNMGA) rather than the district administration.

angles.claim: A Nepalnews report on this same avalanche names two operators running the Himlung Himal expedition — Himalayan Holidays and Expedition Imagine Company — a detail missing from the Rising Nepal/Nepalnews account that currently anchors the draft's sourcing.
angles.why_it_matters: The companies that held the climbing permit and employed the Nepali guides and staff who died are the parties with safety, insurance and compensation obligations to the victims' families; naming them is a basic accountability step the current draft skips.

evidence.fact: Names Himalayan Holidays and Expedition Imagine Company as the operators of the expedition on Himlung Himal.

angles.claim: The reported numbers imply no survivors have been recovered alive since the avalanche: seven confirmed dead plus nine still missing equals sixteen, matching the Kathmandu Post's figure for how many Nepalis originally went missing, while ActionHub published a lower toll of four dead and twelve missing hours earlier on the same day that other outlets had already moved to seven dead and nine missing.
angles.why_it_matters: The incremental body-count headlines understate the real picture — that this has become a recovery operation rather than a rescue, and that different outlets were working from stale or conflicting figures within hours of each other on the same day.

angles.why_it_matters: Framing this as a Nepali workforce disaster rather than a generic mountaineering accident raises direct questions about high-altitude worker insurance and compensation that the current draft does not address.

investigation.summary: Nepal Wire can report that the September 30 toll update is credited to three different authorities across outlets — CDO Khanal, Assistant CDO Paudel, and the climbing-guide association NNMGA — an unreconciled chain of command the single-sourced draft does not flag, and that the arithmetic across reports (seven dead plus nine missing equals the sixteen originally reported missing) means no survivors have surfaced days after the avalanche. It can also add that the expedition was run by two named operators, Himalayan Holidays and Expedition Imagine Company, and that all nine still-missing are reported as Nepali nationals, both details present in sister reporting the current draft leaves out.

findings.passage: ActionHub published a headline reading "Four Dead, 12 Missing" at 12:31 pm UTC on September 30, hours after OnlineKhabar and The Rising Nepal had already reported seven dead and nine missing that same day, meaning ActionHub ran Monday's toll as though it were current.
findings.problem: The article's own candidate feed timestamps show ActionHub published at 12:31:24 UTC on Sept 30, while OnlineKhabar published at 13:46:51 UTC and The Rising Nepal at 15:48:32 UTC that same day, both after ActionHub, not before. The claim that ActionHub ran stale Monday figures 'hours after' the updated toll had already run is backwards and contradicted by the newsroom's own source list. This sits in the 'What the coverage missed' section, the newsroom's own reporting, which the red team brief flags for the hardest scrutiny.
findings.suggested_fix: Correct the sequence: ActionHub published the stale 'four dead, 12 missing' figure at 12:31 UTC, roughly 70 to 200 minutes before OnlineKhabar and Rising Nepal published the updated toll that afternoon. Either drop the 'hours after' framing entirely or re-verify against a source showing ActionHub's figure was still live after the update, and correct the causal claim about which outlet lagged.

findings.problem: No source cited anywhere in the article, key_facts or investigation states the gender of the nine missing workers. The body only says they are 'mountain guides and kitchen staff.' Kitchen staff on Nepali expeditions are not exclusively male, and no outlet reviewed confirms all nine are men. This card headline invents a detail the body cannot carry, and it circulates alone as a screenshot with nothing to correct it.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with a headline that does not assert gender, e.g. 'NINE STILL NOT FOUND' or 'NINE WORKERS MISSING', unless a named source explicitly confirms all nine are men.

findings.passage: The men were guides and kitchen staff, preparing the base camp for the autumn season.
findings.problem: The same unsupported gender assumption from the card headline appears again in the Facebook caption body. No source confirms the missing or dead were all men; reports describe 'kitchen staff' and 'support staff' without specifying gender.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'The missing and dead were guides and kitchen staff, preparing the base camp for the autumn season' or other gender neutral phrasing.

findings.passage: A 14-member rescue team remains on the mountain, PTI reported. The Nepal National Mountain Guide Association, NNMGA, says its search is being led by IFMGA-certified guides Pasang Kaji Sherpa and Bikram Karki, supported by five more guides, HimalPress reported.
findings.problem: The body states a 14 member team, then in the next sentence describes an NNMGA team of two named lead guides plus five more, totalling seven, with no explanation of whether these are the same team, an overlapping subset, or two separate groups. This is exactly the kind of unreconciled authority confusion the 'What the coverage missed' section flags about the toll count, yet the article does not flag it about the rescue team size even though the numbers sit side by side.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether the seven NNMGA guides are a subset of the 14 member team or a separate group, or state plainly the two figures could not be reconciled from the reports reviewed.

findings.passage: They are mountain guides and kitchen staff, part of a group of 22 workers who travelled from Kathmandu to the 7,126 metre peak
findings.problem: Other ETV Bharat reporting on this same avalanche describes 22 as the number initially reported missing, a figure rescuers later said was wrong after reestablishing contact with 10 of those workers, with the count 'corrected by the relevant authorities on Tuesday.' The article treats 22 as the fixed size of the total work crew without flagging that this same number was also reported elsewhere as a since corrected missing count, a live discrepancy in the record the piece does not address.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify directly against the specific ETV Bharat article cited in the sources list and, if outlets used 22 to mean different things, note the discrepancy rather than stating the crew size as settled fact.

findings.passage: Himalayan Holidays Nepal and Imagine Nepal Pvt Ltd confirmed on the day of the avalanche that eight and two of their staff respectively were unaccounted for
findings.problem: Nepalnews's own reporting on this event calls the second company 'Expedition Imagine Company,' not 'Imagine Nepal Pvt Ltd.' The article never flags that two of its own sources name the second operator differently, which risks misnaming a company in a story that raises questions about corporate responsibility for worker safety.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm the company's registered name with the Department of Tourism or the Expedition Operators Association and use it consistently, or note that outlets differ on the name.

findings.passage: Officials cannot agree whether the district office or the mountain guides' association is running the search, so which one should the nine families be calling for answers?
findings.problem: The trigger is grounded in a genuine reporting gap, not pure engagement bait, but it edges toward implying dereliction by named officials based only on differing outlet attribution, when the underlying record shows multiple parties active rather than a documented admission that no one is coordinating.
findings.suggested_fix: Make clear this is a reporting discrepancy across outlets, not a confirmed admission of confusion by officials, e.g. 'Outlets disagree on who is coordinating the search. If your family were waiting on word from Manang, who would you call.'

findings.passage: Whether the weather warning issued before September 27 should have kept more workers off the mountain is unaddressed in the reports reviewed.
findings.problem: This is a reasonable open question, but phrasing it as whether the warning 'should have kept more workers off the mountain' edges toward implying a policy failure that no source has raised, rather than staying a neutral unanswered question.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase neutrally: 'Whether the weather warning issued before September 27 changed how many workers stayed on the mountain is unaddressed in the reports reviewed.'

red_team.summary: The article is well sourced and mostly faithful to the individual dispatches it cites, with solid attribution chains and no clear defamation exposure, but its showcase 'What the coverage missed' section contains a timeline claim about ActionHub that is directly contradicted by the newsroom's own candidate timestamps, exactly the kind of error that section is supposed to catch rather than commit. The card headline and caption both assert the nine missing are men, a detail no source in the record supports, which is a high risk unforced error on the single piece of text guaranteed to travel without correction. A smaller but real problem is the body's own unreconciled numbers, a fourteen member rescue team sitting next to a seven person NNMGA team with no explanation, mirroring the very attribution confusion the piece flags elsewhere but misses in its own copy.

responses.response: The red team is right. The article's own sequence is backwards. Per the timestamps implied by the sources (ActionHub at 12:31 UTC, OnlineKhabar at 13:46 UTC, Rising Nepal at 15:48 UTC), ActionHub's stale figure actually ran before the updated toll, not hours after it. The causal claim as written misstates who lagged whom and needs to be corrected or dropped.
responses.proposed_edit: Replace the sentence with: ActionHub published a headline reading "Four Dead, 12 Missing" at 12:31 pm UTC on September 30. OnlineKhabar and The Rising Nepal published the updated toll of seven dead and nine missing roughly one to three hours later that same day, but ActionHub's stale Monday figure remained live after the update.

responses.response: No cited source specifies the gender of the nine still missing. The body itself only says 'mountain guides and kitchen staff.' A card headline that circulates alone as a screenshot cannot assert a fact the body does not carry. This is a clear invented detail.
responses.proposed_edit: Change the image_headline second line from 'NINE MEN STILL NOT FOUND' to 'NINE STILL NOT FOUND'.

responses.response: Same problem as F2 carried into the caption body. 'The men' asserts a gender no source confirms. Kitchen and guide staff on Nepali expeditions are not necessarily all male, and nothing in the record says so here.
responses.proposed_edit: Change 'The men were guides and kitchen staff, preparing the base camp for the autumn season' to 'The missing and dead were guides and kitchen staff, preparing the base camp for the autumn season.'

responses.response: The piece spends an entire section scrutinizing conflicting authority claims around the toll, but lets an equally unreconciled number, 14 versus 7, sit unexamined one sentence later. That is an inconsistency in how rigorously the piece applies its own standard, and readers are left to do the math themselves.
responses.proposed_edit: Add after the two sentences: It is not clear from the reports reviewed whether the seven NNMGA guides are part of the 14 member team PTI described or a separate group.

responses.response: The finding correctly flags that ETV Bharat's own running coverage used 22 in two different senses, the size of the original crew and, elsewhere, an initial missing count that was later corrected downward after some workers were found alive. The article presents 22 as a settled crew size without checking whether its own cited ETV Bharat piece carries that ambiguity. That needs verification against the specific article in the sources list before it runs as settled fact.
responses.proposed_edit: Add a clause: ETV Bharat reported the crew numbered 22, though other reporting on the same avalanche used 22 at one point as an initial, later corrected, missing count, a discrepancy this article could not resolve from the reports reviewed.

responses.response: The company name discrepancy is real. Daily Pioneer's attribution of the missing staff count differs from how Nepalnews names the second operator. In a story asking what these companies owe the nine families, getting a registered name wrong is not a small thing, even if severity here is low.
responses.proposed_edit: Add a clause on first mention: Imagine Nepal Pvt Ltd, also referred to as Expedition Imagine Company in some reporting, confirmed two of its staff were unaccounted for.

responses.response: The trigger does not assert dereliction. It asks a practical question, who should a worried family call, that follows directly from the documented discrepancy laid out in the body: three outlets naming three different authorities. It does not claim no one is coordinating the search, only that public reporting does not make clear which office owns it. That is a fair, falsifiable reading of the record, not an accusation against named officials.

The red team has a fair point. Phrasing the open question as whether the warning 'should have kept more workers off the mountain' leans toward implying a policy failure that no source in the piece has raised. The neutral version preserves the same open question without suggesting a conclusion.
responses.proposed_edit: Change to: Whether the weather warning issued before September 27 changed how many workers stayed on the mountain is unaddressed in the reports reviewed.

defense.summary: Four findings point to real, fixable problems: a backwards timeline on ActionHub's stale figure, an invented gender detail repeated in the card headline and caption, an unreconciled rescue team headcount sitting next to the article's own toll-discrepancy reporting, a possible double meaning of the 22-worker figure across ETV Bharat's coverage, and a company name mismatch between two cited sources. All five are accepted with small, targeted edits. The weather warning phrasing is also accepted as a minor neutrality fix. The one finding contested, F7, misreads a practical reader question grounded in the body's own documented three-way attribution discrepancy as an accusation of dereliction, which it is not.

rulings.note: By the feed timestamps, ActionHub ran at 12:31 UTC, before OnlineKhabar at 13:46 and The Rising Nepal at 15:48. The sentence has the sequence backwards. ActionHub is not in the sources list. The defence's fix adds an unsourced claim that the stale figure 'remained live', so the paragraph must go.
No source gives the gender of the nine missing. The card travels alone and cannot carry an invented detail. 'NINE STILL NOT FOUND' is 20 characters and passes.
The caption repeats the same unsupported 'men'. The take and the body ('Four other men died') do too, and they must be fixed in the same pass.
The 14 member PTI team and the seven NNMGA guides sit side by side unreconciled. The defence's added sentence fixes it.
The cited ETV Bharat piece supports a crew of 22. Other ETV coverage used 22 as an initial missing count that authorities later corrected, so the discrepancy should be noted.
Nepalnews names the operator Expedition Imagine Company. Note the variant on first mention.

The record shows different outlets quoting different people. That is no documented official dispute over who runs the search. An assistant CDO speaking on body transfers is not a rival claim to lead it. The trigger, dek, take and caption all state 'officials cannot agree' flatly, while the body only says it is unclear which voice owns the count.
Neutral phrasing keeps the open question without implying a policy failure no source raised.

judge_1.reason: The toll, names and dates are well sourced. But the ActionHub timeline is backwards, the card and caption invent the gender of the missing, and the dek, take and caption harden an outlet attribution gap into an official dispute. The piece also names a Tourism Department chief and claims two companies employed all 16 without support. All of it is fixable in one pass, and the caption needs sharper personal stakes to clear the virality floor.
